research_question: Is the non-monotonic numerical error across hierarchical QFourier architectures explained by a trade-off between accumulation in stage 1 and accumulation in the stage-2 head?
observations: For width 4, logit MAE improved from 4 to 8 to 16 groups but worsened at 28 groups.
More groups reduce pixels per first-stage block while increasing the number of intermediate features consumed by the head.
hypothesis: Stage-1 reference-to-Q.ANT error will generally fall as input groups become smaller, while stage-2 error contribution will eventually grow as the head receives more intermediate features; their combination will explain the observed minimum near the middle of the tested group-count range.
falsification_criterion: The hypothesis is weakened if stage-local errors do not show the predicted opposing trends or if their measured behavior cannot account for the non-monotonic final-logit error.
limitations: CPU backend only; no photonic hardware performance claim.
Stage-local error metrics are diagnostic decompositions and need not add linearly because the second stage is nonlinear.
